newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices slightly up, low mill buying.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices slightly up, low mill buying.

text.p: Indian cotton prices on Wednesday gained slightly following reports that the Indian government has allowed more exports of cotton yarn, dealers said.
In spot deals Bengal-deshi rose by 10 rupees at 900/930 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned rose by 25 rupees at 1,550/1,660 rupees per maund.
Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) lifted by 100 rupees at 13,300/13,500 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).
"More export of cotton yarn will lead to more buying of cotton by the spinning mills," a broker said.
Arrivals of cotton also remained low at producing centres on account of unseasonal rain and cloudy weather.
"Out of the cotton crop of 16 million bales for the 1996/1997, about 14/14.50 million bales ( 170 kg each) have already been sold," he said.
